title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook — Comprehensive
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s canonical on-call and incident response practices: severity definitions, responder roles, escalation policies, runbooks for common failure modes, postmortem and communication templates, on-call rotation rules, and game-day guidance. It is intended for SREs, on-call engineers, product/feature owners, customer success, and any stakeholders involved in incident management.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Applies to all production services provided by Redwood Inference (hosted API, routing layer, runtime, dedicated control plane).
- Audience: on-call SREs, service owners, support, product, and engineering managers.

Key contacts and ownership
--------------------------
- Incident Response Owner: Eng SRE Team (eng-sre@redwood.com)
- Incident Commander (IC): assigned at incident start (see Roles)
- Communications Lead: Customer Success (cs-comms@redwood.com) for customer-facing messages; Eng SRE for internal comms

Severity definitions (SEV)
-------------------------
1. SEV1 — Major outage: service unavailable or significant data loss affecting >25% of customers or critical internal systems. Immediate 24/7 response.
2. SEV2 — Partial outage / severe degradation: request latency or errors significantly above SLO affecting key customers or features. Requires immediate response during business hours and on-call after-hours.
3. SEV3 — Degraded experience / intermittent errors: elevated error rates or degraded performance impacting a small subset of users or non-critical flows.
4. SEV4 — Informational / minor issue: non-urgent alerts, performance concerns with no customer impact.

SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)
-----------------------------------
- API availability SLO: 99.95% monthly.
- Critical request 99th percentile latency: 300ms target, 500ms alert threshold.
- Error rate alert: 0.5% 1m error rate (warning), 1.5% 1m error rate (critical).
- Backend queue depth: >10k pending messages triggers paging.

Roles & responsibilities
------------------------
- Incident Commander (IC): Central coordinator for the incident. Owns the timeline, decisions, and post-incident review.
- SRE On-call (Primary): Responsible for initial triage, mitigation steps, and executing runbooks.
- SRE Backup (Secondary): Escalation target if primary is unavailable or needs assistance.
- Service Owner / Eng Lead: Technical authority for the affected service; provides fixes and prioritizes rollouts.
- Communications Lead: Manages internal and external (status page) messages.
- Customer Success (CS): Coordinates with customers and shares impact/ETA when appropriate.
- Incident Note-taker: Captures timeline, actions, and decisions in the incident document.

Alerting and paging policy
-------------------------
1. Alerts originate from monitoring (Prometheus/Alertmanager, Datadog) and the runtime telemetry pipeline.
2. Pager escalation: Primary -> 10 minutes -> Secondary -> 15 minutes -> ESCALATE to IC/On-call manager and Eng Lead.
3. For SEV1/SEV2: immediate page to primary and a Slack channel is created automatically (#incident-YYYYMMDD-XXXX).
4. For lower severities, use tickets and async communication unless the situation escalates.

Incident lifecycle (step-by-step)
--------------------------------
1. Detection and Triage
   - Acknowledge alert in Alertmanager/Datadog.
   - Create an incident channel and incident document (use template below).
   - IC declares severity and documents initial hypotheses.
2. Containment / Mitigation
   - Apply short-term mitigations to reduce customer impact (traffic limits, rollback, config toggle).
   - If mitigation requires cross-team coordination, IC contacts Eng Lead and CS.
3. Diagnosis
   - Collect logs, traces, and metrics. Prioritize data sources: request traces -> host metrics -> kernel/GPU metrics -> network telemetry.
   - Reproduce the issue in staging if safe.
4. Remediation / Recovery
   - Implement fix (code change, configuration, or infrastructure action).
   - Validate recovery via automated health checks and canary traffic.
5. Communication
   - Post initial status on internal channel and open status.redwoood.com (internal status tooling) and public status page if customer-visible.
   - Update cadence: Every 15 minutes for SEV1 until stable; every 30–60 minutes for SEV2.
6. Close & Review
   - Declare incident resolved when service meets SLOs for 30 minutes and root cause identified or mitigated.
   - IC schedules postmortem within 48 hours (see Postmortem template).

Runbooks (operational examples)
------------------------------
Note: Runbook steps assume access to kubectl / private CLI and internal dashboards. Always capture commands and outputs in the incident doc.

1) API Gateway Full Outage (SEV1)
- Symptoms: 5xx on inbound requests across regions; monitoring shows gateway error rate > 10%.
- Immediate mitigation steps:
  1. Page SRE On-call and create incident channel.
  2. Check ingress controller pods: kubectl -n gateway get pods -o wide
  3. Check gateway logs for OOM / panic signatures: kubectl -n gateway logs <pod> --since=10m
  4. If pod crashlooping, scale down to 0 and scale up new version with image tag pinned: kubectl -n gateway scale deploy/gateway --replicas=3
  5. If config change triggered outage, revert last config commit: /ops/config-revert --service gateway --to HEAD~1
  6. If mitigation applied, verify 200 responses via: curl -sSf https://api.redwood.com/health || true
- Escalation: If service not recovered in 10 minutes, escalate to Eng Lead and consider diverting traffic to a fallback endpoint.

2) Model Runtime Elevated GPU OOMs (SEV2)
- Symptoms: increased model eviction, memory spikes, GPU OOMs, requests failing with 503.
- Mitigation steps:
  1. Identify affected node(s): query telemetry: label=gpu, metric=gpu_free_memory
  2. Drain problematic node: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
  3. Reconfigure batch sizes or apply conservative quantization profile via runtime flags: "--batch_max_tokens=512 --quant_profile=cpu-friendly"
  4. If bug related to model weights, rollback to previous model variant (see model-onboarding rollback playbook).

Runbook guidelines
- Always capture exact commands and outputs.
- Include checklist items: customer impact, mitigation applied, timeline entry.
- If executing destructive actions (drain, scale down), coordinate with IC.

Postmortem template (blameless)
--------------------------------
Fields to complete within 72 hours of incident resolution:
- Title (one-liner)
- Incident ID / channel: #incident-YYYYMMDD-XXXX
- Severity: SEV1/2/3
- Summary: What happened (2–3 sentences)
- Impact: systems and customers affected, duration, estimated business impact
- Timeline: ordered list of key events with timestamps (UTC)
- Root cause: one-sentence root cause statement
- Contributing factors: environment, process, tooling gaps
- Resolution and mitigation: what was done to resolve
- Post-incident actions (P0/P1/P2): concrete tasks, owners, and due dates
- Lessons learned and follow-ups: training, instrumentation, process changes
- Attachments: logs, graphs, dashboards, rollbacks, PRs

Acceptance criteria for postmortem:
- Postmortem drafted within 72 hours, reviewed by Eng Lead and SRE manager.
- P0 actions identified and scheduled within 7 days.

On-call rotations and handoffs
-----------------------------
- Primary rotation: 1 week on-call (Mon 09:00 UTC -> next Mon 09:00 UTC) or 7×24 split depending on team rules.
- Overnight/night coverage: follows the same primary; teams may run 12-hour shifts for high-volume teams.
- Handoff procedure:
  1. Outgoing takes 15-minute overlap with incoming.
  2. Outgoing reviews active alerts, ongoing incidents, and open P0/P1 actions with incoming.
  3. Update on-call calendar and Slack status.
- Vacation / backup requests: on-call swaps must be recorded in the on-call calendar and notify the on-call manager at least 24 hours in advance.

Game days (practice incidents)
-----------------------------
- Frequency: Quarterly for each platform area (runtime, gateway, control plane).
- Goals: validate runbooks, improve team coordination, exercise cross-team comms and public comms.
- Typical scenarios:
  - Multi-region failover (simulate networking partition)
  - High-error-rate injection on routing layer
  - Model cold-cache recovery and KV cache corruption
- Post-game-day: run a retrospective and produce action items with owners.

Status page & customer communications templates
---------------------------------------------
Public status messages should be clear, non-technical, and contain impact/ETA when known. Internal status may contain technical context.

1) Investigating (initial)
- Public: "We are investigating reports of errors affecting the Redwood API. Our engineering team is investigating and we'll provide updates every 15 minutes."
- Internal: "SEV2: Elevated 5xx rate on API gateway beginning 2026-02-10T14:12Z. IC: @Aisha. Triage in progress."

2) Identified / Degraded performance
- Public: "We have identified a problem causing degraded performance for a subset of requests. We have a mitigation in place and are monitoring while we implement a fix."
- Internal: Include link to incident doc, cause hypothesis, mitigation steps, and next actions.

3) Partial outage / Major outage
- Public: "We are experiencing a partial outage affecting some API requests. Our engineers are working on a fix and we will provide updates every 15 minutes. If you are a paid customer experiencing critical impact, contact support@redwood.com."

4) Resolved
- Public: "The issue has been resolved. We’re continuing to monitor and will follow up with a post-incident report. We apologize for the disruption."

Communication cadence and channels
---------------------------------
- Channels: PagerDuty/Alertmanager -> Slack (#incidents) -> Incident doc (Confluence) -> Status page -> Customer email (CS)
- Cadence: 15m updates during SEV1, 30–60m for SEV2; ad-hoc for lower SEVs.

Metrics to capture during incidents
---------------------------------
- Error rate, 5xx ratio, p50/p95/p99 latency, request throughput, pod restart counts, GPU memory usage, queue depth.

Review & continuous improvement
--------------------------------
- Monthly on-call retro: review recent incidents, identify systemic issues, and triage postmortem action items into backlog.
- Quarterly runbook audit: service owners must validate their runbooks and update commands/contacts.

Appendix: Incident document template (Confluence-friendly)
---------------------------------------------------------
- Title: [SEV][Service] Short description
- Incident ID / Channel: #incident-YYYYMMDD-XXXX
- Summary: 2–3 sentences
- Severity: SEV1/2/3/4
- Impact: bullet list of affected customers/features
- Timeline: table or ordered bullets with timestamps (UTC)
- Actions taken: bullets with actor and timestamp
- Current status: investigating / mitigation / resolved
- Next steps: owners & due dates
- Postmortem link: (link to postmortem page)

FAQ and edge cases
------------------
- If an alert pages the wrong team: swap ownership in PagerDuty and notify IC.
- If a third-party provider is root cause: gather evidence, notify vendor, and draft customer-facing statement with CS.
- If a security incident is suspected: treat as high priority and notify Security (security@redwood.com) immediately; do not post public details until coordinated with Security.

Document maintenance
--------------------
- Owner: Eng SRE.
- Review cadence: annual review and after any SEV1 incident.
- How to propose changes: open a PR against this Confluence page and add reviewer from Eng SRE.

Related pages and runbooks
-------------------------
- Runtime runbooks: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks
- Model onboarding rollback: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding
- SLOs and error budgets: /confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets

This playbook is deliberately prescriptive: runbooks must be followed, communications must be timely, and postmortems must drive corrective work. For questions or suggested improvements, contact the Eng SRE owner.
